properties.description:
The surplus half of DETECT. Every existing gap asks what is MISSING; this asks what is SURPLUS — realized or verified, and downstream of nothing.

THE SIGNAL, computable from the graph as it stands: a Capability at `realized`/`verified` with no incoming DEPENDS_ON, no PART_OF_FLOW into any Flow, and no Actor INTERACTS_WITH. The same shape generalises to a Component whose Interfaces nothing CONSUMES, and to an Artifact realizing only capabilities that are themselves unconsumed.

⚠️ THE WORDING IS THE FEATURE, not a caveat on it. The graph knows DESIGN-LEVEL demand and nothing about runtime usage, so the honest finding is \"NOTHING IN THIS DESIGN CONSUMES X\" — never \"X is unused\". A feature real users call daily whose consumer was never modelled produces exactly the same graph shape as a dead one, and a detector that did not say so would confidently recommend deleting working code. Reported as a FACT rather than a gap for the same reason granularity_report and surprising_connections are: which side is wrong is the user's to say.

WHY IT IS NOT unmotivated_capability: that fires on a capability satisfying no REQUIREMENT — a question about intent, gated on requirements existing at all. A capability can satisfy a requirement perfectly and still be consumed by nothing, and that is the expensive case, because the paperwork is complete and the code is dead.

DELIBERATELY NOT COVERED HERE: runtime usage. dec:bl-155 and dec:idea-measure-the-surface hold that question, and answering it needs telemetry rather than the graph.
properties.name: A built thing that nothing in the design consumes is surfaced, and says so as a design-completeness finding rather than a verdict on the system
